sources.entry: Loki | Horizontally scalable log aggregation system

summary.one_liner: Loki is a horizontally scalable, multi-tenant log aggregation system inspired by Prometheus that indexes only log labels rather than log contents.
summary.what_it_does: Loki stores compressed, unstructured logs and indexes only a set of labels per log stream, instead of doing full-text indexing. It uses the same label model as Prometheus so users can move between metrics and logs with the same labels. Logs are delivered by push rather than pull. The README describes a three-part stack: Alloy as the agent that collects logs and sends them to Loki, Loki itself for storage and queries, and Grafana for querying and display. It can run as a single binary with no dependencies, and it can be run with multiple tenants when auth is enabled. The README also lists related tools: Docker Driver Client for sending container logs, LogCLI for command-line queries, and Loki Canary for detecting missing logs.
use_cases: sending Docker container logs to a central store
how_to_run: git clone the loki repository and cd into it
Alternatively, on Unix systems: make loki
For multi-tenant local runs: set auth_enabled to true and run ./loki with loki-local-multi-tenant-config.yaml and loki-overrides.yaml
notable: Indexes labels only, not log contents, which keeps storage and operation cheap
Multi-tenant mode with runtime config overrides
Uses Prometheus-style label model to link metrics and logs
caveats: The README notes Promtail has been replaced by Alloy for log collection, and Promtail is feature complete
The Helm chart is moving to a separate grafana-community repository effective March 16, 2026; the Loki repo chart is maintained only for GEL users
Native Grafana support is described as needing Grafana v6.0 or later
Building from source requires an up-to-date version of Go
